items.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah. Basie at the piano just like — [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. He was barely doing anything he was just like one-two-three-four off you go.

ctx.x: some energy. Like Ray Wright — I don’t know, or sorry, Ray Ricker — Ray Wright’s dead. Ray Ricker was at a concert, or he watched a concert the other night and he wrote me a note and he said, “I love your minimalistic conducting. It’s not like you’re like the wind symphony conductors where you have to direct everything.” And I said, “You don’t need to direct everything in jazz.” I mean it depends on context a lot but if the rhythm keeps the pulse of what’s going on, and it’s well rehearsed, you barely have to do…
Yeah. Basie at the piano just like —

Yeah. He was barely doing anything he was just like one-two-three-four off you go. And yeah, I think the jazz repertoire for large ensemble is evolving all the time rhythmically and you know using different meters and things. So it gets complicated. It’s all time and place and what are we going to do. But I have to say when I took my band on tour, the one opportunity I got to go across Canada, by day three I did not need to stand in front of that band so I just started picking up my horn and playing melodies with…
